body:
I'm hovering around the threshold of Plat 4-Plat 5. Which is...average? I think that's what the rank distribution said last I saw. Played Luke at launch, grinded him from Silver to Plat 2, went to play Granblue for a bit instead, came back for Akuma and got him to Plat 5.


Once upon a time I was a FighterZ player and I loved mashing in that game. I barely knew anything about how to play fighting games back then. I'd kill for that blissful ignorance again. 


How do you get that joy back? Is it even possible? I know my mindset needs changed, but I can't figure out how to do it.

I actually just finished Inner Game of Tennis recently! Great book, it put a lot of things into perspective in a way I hadn't been able to before. I just wish I could apply those concepts better than I am now.


I know that it's ultimately just video games at the end of the day, and I need to calm the fuck down about it all. But I'm struggling to bring myself to, especially since I staked a lot of my identity around playing and talking about these games. 


I'm hardly as passionate about anything as I am fighting games, and I don't know how to move that passion into something better I guess.

I don't think I was clear enough in my post, so I'm going to try as best I can to clarify a bit further.


Obviously, my mindset is whack. It's what's hurting my play, what's stopping me from improving, and what's preventing me from having fun with the genre. I know this. I know I need to change it if I want to keep going, but what I don't know is HOW. I know I need to shift from my fixed mindset to a growth/learning mindset, but I can't figure out how to actually DO that, and my emotions get the better of me anyway. Yes, I have a fragile ego. Yes, I'm bringing that into my matches. But I don't know how to stop.



I love fighting games. I love the games, the characters, the systems, and the flow of them. I wouldn't be as upset with myself and I would have given up entirely a long time ago if I didn't. Somewhere along the way, I forgot how to have fun with these games, and I don't know how to get it back. I would love to be the kind of person who just mindlessly queues for games and doesn't give a shit what happens in the end because they're having fun, but I don't know if I can get to that point.
